name: Anathema-Vortex
specific_features: Signal of unknown origin from beneath the storm decks
Derelict space station (Veilwatch Prime, broadcasting quarantine)
description: Anathema-Vortex fills a fifth of the local sky, a banded colossus of amber and bruise-purple wrapped in storms wider than most empires. Its rings are young and wrong, glittering with fresh debris, and the great red vortex at the southern tropic has rotated without pause for as long as records exist.

Nothing about close approach feels natural. The magnetic anomalies twist compass readings into knots, radio traffic returns doubled and half a second late, and pilots report the sensation of the planet watching rather than merely turning. In the shadow bands, the storm tops glow faintly, though no sun reaches them there.

Veilwatch Prime was built to skim helium-3 from the upper decks, until the night its crew reported a signal rising from far below the cloud bases, structured, patient, and repeating. Contact ceased mid-transmission; the station has run on automation ever since, sweeping the approach lanes with quarantine warnings no authority admits to programming. Whatever answered from below has never identified itself, and has never stopped.

The perimeter beacons mark a mined exclusion shell that has claimed three smugglers this decade alone, yet the fuel in those amber belts is worth a fleet. Every year some consortium petitions to reopen the skim routes, and every year the petition dies quietly after a survey ship spends one night listening to the signal climb.
